title: cc connections --json
description: The organization's declared service roster (projected from cli-copilot foundation's `copilot --json layers` services[], >=schema_version 1 with the id/requires_secret/store_scope addition) plus, per service, whether its declared credential names are present (never their values) in the organization's shared Infisical store. Computed entirely CLI-side (invariant #1: parse, never compute) -- Control Tower renders the roster and filters into its two card groups (READY TO USE / AVAILABLE TO CONNECT) using `connections[].secret_state` alone. See docs/01-architecture/cli-contract.md and claude-copilot/tools/cc/src/cc/commands/connections.py's module docstring for the full design (WP-388/389/390, task 221).

result.description: Envelope-level outcome, distinct per fail-closed reason rather than a generic error bucket. 'copilot-unavailable': the `copilot` binary could not be resolved/run, or returned an unreadable/unfamiliar report -- `connections` is empty because the service roster itself could not be enumerated. 'org-config-unavailable': the inherited `ecosystem.yml` was not found on this Mac -- `connections` is STILL populated from `copilot --json layers` alone (tier/mode/requires_secret do not depend on the org config), but `store.reachable` is false and every row needing a store-checkable secret reads `secret_state: "no-store"`. 'ok': normal operation; `store.reachable` and each row's `secret_state` carry any further degradation. This field is a diagnostic for the app to log/report, not something the app should filter connections on -- that is `connections[].secret_state`'s job alone.

detail.description: Plain-language reason, present whenever `result` is not "ok"; null when `result` is "ok".

org.description: The organization name from the inherited `ecosystem.yml` (`org:` key), or null when unknown (no org config materialized, or it lacks an `org` key).

type.description: The org's declared shared-store type (`ecosystem.yml` `store.type`, e.g. "infisical"), or null when unknown.

reachable.description: True only after a real presence-check call against the store succeeded. False whenever the store is unconfigured, deferred, of an unsupported type, or unreachable on this Mac -- never assumed true.

scope.description: Non-secret `environment:secret_path` summary of where this run looked (e.g. "prod:/shared"). Never includes the opaque workspace id or any credential. Null when the org config does not declare a usable environment/secret_path.

detail.description: Plain-language reason the store is not reachable, or null when reachable (or when nothing further to report).

connections.description: One row per `copilot --json layers` service, in that payload's own order. Empty only when `result` is "copilot-unavailable" (the roster itself could not be read).

id.description: Stable slug (cli-copilot's `services[].id`, or `name` when the installed `copilot` predates that field).

name.description: The `copilot <name>` command group -- this row's identity for a Connect action to reference.

tier.description: Which layer id this service resolves from (cli-copilot's `services[].tier`), e.g. "org-internal" or "foundation".

mode.description: Same vocabulary as cli-copilot's `services[].mode`: 'base' untouched foundation service, 'adopt' a tier turned on a base service with its own config/secrets, 'override' a tier replaced the implementation, 'provides' a tier added a service the base 12 do not have at all.

requires_secret.description: Every credential NAME this service declares, in declaration order. Names only, never values. Empty when the service declares none.

store_scope.description: This service's declared store scope (maps to the org's `ecosystem.yml` `team_scopes`), passed through verbatim. Null when the declaring tier's overlay entry does not set one -- the common case today (the real org's `team_scopes` is currently empty).

secret_state.description: 'ready': no `store`/`any`-hinted secret is required, or every one required is present in the shared store (a service with only `keychain`-hinted secrets, or none at all, is `ready` -- there is nothing for the shared store to prove). 'needs-connect': the store is reachable but at least one required `store`/`any`-hinted secret name is absent from it -- see `missing`. 'no-store': the shared store itself is unreachable/unconfigured, so no `store`/`any`-hinted secret required by this row could be verified -- distinct from `needs-connect` (a store problem, not a per-secret gap).

missing.description: Secret NAMES (never values) this row still needs, in `requires_secret` order. Empty when `secret_state` is "ready"; every store/any-hinted required name when `secret_state` is "no-store" (none could be verified); the specific absent subset when `secret_state` is "needs-connect".

requiredSecret.description: Byte-identical shape to cli-copilot's own `$defs.requiredSecret` (docs/schemas/layers.schema.json) -- duplicated here (a different repo/schema file) rather than cross-referenced, since Control Tower never resolves a cli-copilot-hosted $ref at runtime.

name.description: The credential name resolved via the credential ladder. Never a value.

from.description: Routing hint restricting which credential-ladder rungs are tried for this name. 'any' is the default when the declaring tier's overlay entry is a bare string name (tries every rung). This verb presence-checks only `store`/`any`-hinted names against the shared store; `keychain`-hinted names are excluded from `secret_state`/`missing` computation (see `connections.schema.json`'s own `secret_state` description).
